mutations.note: BROAD BY NATURE, and the exact observed set. Diffing by argv path instead of blob SHA makes git compare WORKTREE to INDEX; after the fixtures' `git add -A` those are identical, so hunksFor returns no hunks for any staged change and the guard misses every retraction. That is why most of the suites redden. The argv-specific consequence the comment names — a name carrying raw bytes re-encoded on its way through argv — is the odd-byte fixture alone. A narrower form was measured and rejected: appending `-- entry.path` to the blob-to-blob diff makes git reject the pathspec and the guard exits 2 (could-not-run), grading nothing. Cascade exposure: any test added to these suites that this break also reddens will MISMATCH this entry until the set is re-derived. The harness catches a stale set before merge — re-derive with `node .claude/hooks/run-mutations.mjs --guard check-retracted-phrase` and take the observed set.

notEncoded.claim: reorder FILE_EXT so "ts" precedes "tsx" → "quiz-config-form.tsx" matches as "quiz-config-form.ts", a file that may not exist, inverting the existence tier's verdict. (check-retracted-phrase.test.mjs, test "does not split a .tsx filename into a .ts one")
notEncoded.why: SURVIVED — the comment overclaims. Applying exactly that reorder (FILE_EXT = [ts, tsx, jsx, ...]) leaves all four suites green: 31/31 and 34/34 pass. FILE_RE's trailing lookahead (?![\w-]) independently rejects the ".ts" partial match and forces the regex to backtrack into "tsx". Removing the lookahead ALONE is also green, because longest-first ordering then does the work. The test is pinned only by the CONJUNCTION: removing both (ts-first order AND the lookahead) is the one edit that reddens it, and reddens exactly it. (The source comment that carried the same overclaim was CORRECTED on this branch; the quote is not repeated here so it cannot outlive the fix.)

notEncoded.claim: remove escapeRe from reAdded → the dot in 'plan.md' becomes a regex wildcard; 'planXmd' satisfies both boundaries and the retraction is falsely exonerated. (check-retracted-phrase.test.mjs, test "reAdded: a dot inside a filename token is treated as a literal character, not a wildcard")
notEncoded.why: NARROWED twice. The original rationale said no find/replace exists — wrong; the harness replaces arbitrary source text. The second wording then claimed the boundary-keeping RegExp break 'IS encodable and is pinned by that test', which was ALSO wrong: it was encodable and NOT encoded, so the dot-literal test was graded by nothing while this field asserted otherwise. Found by CR-local round 4 and now closed — the break is encoded as `readded-unescaped-boundary-regexp`, verified CAUGHT with that test as its exact red set. What remains genuinely not encodable is the claim AS THE COMMENT WORDS IT: 'remove escapeRe from reAdded' names a mechanism reAdded does not contain, because it builds no regex at all and delegates to tokensOf. A field whose job is to be honest about coverage carried a false coverage claim through two rewrites; that is the defect this guard exists to catch.
